content:
sofia: Quick sync — we need to nail down ownership for the env-proxy lifecycle across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Specifically: TLS termination, cert rotation, who can restart sidecars during rollouts, and metric provenance. Trying to avoid repeated firefights during canaries.

matt: +1 on clarity. My instinct: Hosted control plane should own cert APIs and rotation, Dedicated should have an operator that delegates to infra team, Private leaves certs to customer KMS but we still provide hooks.

jia: I agree with matt but we should be explicit about the runtime behavior. For example: in Dedicated we must support both control-plane driven rotations (for managed certs) and node-local rotation for air-gapped clusters. Those have different rollback semantics.

oliver: One subtlety — sidecar restart semantics matter for KV cache warmup. If we restart aggressively on cert change, cold tokens will blow latency for a minute. Need a rolling restart policy or live-reload where possible.

sofia: Exactly. Can we draft a minimal expected behavior matrix? e.g., columns: TLS ownership, restart trigger, who can force-restart, metric owner. Keep it executable.

samira: Drafting one now. Proposal takes these rows: Hosted / Dedicated-managed / Dedicated-selfmanaged / Private-customer. For Hosted: TLS owned by Redwood CP, rotation via CP API, restarts: controlled canary rollout by CP, metric provenance: Redwood.

matt: For Dedicated-managed: TLS still Redwood if customer opts into managed certs; otherwise customer provides certs via KMS endpoint. Restarts: operator triggers graceful rolling restarts with drain timeout = 45s.

jia: For Dedicated-selfmanaged: operator exposes hooks but doesn't change certs automatically. Customer is responsible; operator will emit events and health-check gating.

oliver: For Private (VPC/on-prem): we should adopt a hard principle: we never mutate customer keys. We provide a management API that returns validation-only flags and rotation suggestions. Restart = customer-controlled. Metric ownership = customer, with opt-in telemetry to Redwood.

sofia: This reads sensible. Two implementation questions: 1) API shape for rotation requests (simple POST? webhook?), 2) how alerts look when restarts are required but customer chooses not to.

samira: Suggestion: single minimal API: POST /v1/proxy/cert-rotation { "target":"proxy-id", "mode":"validate|rotate|suggest" }. For Private we support only validate & suggest unless customer opts-in. Example: 
```
POST /v1/proxy/cert-rotation
{
  "target": "env-proxy-34",
  "mode": "suggest"
}
```
Response: 200 + human-friendly plan.

matt: Love minimal API. Add an async job pattern and event webhooks: rotation_job_id returned; webhook when complete or fails. For Hosted we auto-enqueue rotate jobs at renewal minus TTL buffer.

deploy-bot: deploy:env-proxy v2.13 started by matt at 2791124000 :rocket:

jia: About metric provenance: we need tags on traces / metrics that encode "ownership:hosted|dedicated|private" and a UUID for the control plane that triggered the change. That helps debug who requested the restart.

oliver: Also include a 'restart-cause' label (e.g., cert-rotation, cfg-change, heartbeat-failure) so SRE runbooks can filter with metric queries.

sofia: Good. One more operational constraint: offline rotation support for Private. We should provide a CLI tool that emits the same validation plan as the API (so customers can run locally). CLI output should be identical JSON to the webhook payload for parity.

samira: Noted. I'll add CLI example in the doc. Also will include suggested drain strategy: prefer live reload, else staggered restart with jitter and health-check gating.

matt: Edge-case: what if customer has custom sidecar image that doesn't support live reload? Operator should detect LivenessProbe failure patterns and fallback to conservative restart sequences. Add that to the matrix.

sofia: Thanks all. Action items: @samira draft the behavior matrix + API spec (including job/webhook examples) by EOD; @jia add metric label schema; @matt write two runbook snippets for Hosted and Dedicated-managed restarts. We'll reconvene in tomorrow architecture sync.

oliver: small nit — include a section on RBAC: who can call rotation API in Dedicated-managed. Likely infra-admin role + legal review for cross-tenant cert ops.

samira: Yep adding RBAC table. Will ping when done. :thumbsup:
